Approach and Rationale
The outgoing TriangleMultiplicativeUpdate (TriMul) operator requires an efficient O(N³) computation through a variadic reduction over the sequence dimension. The core challenge lies in performing the matrix multiplication (GEMM) operation, `out[b, i, j, d] = sum_{k} left[b, i, k, d] * right[b, j, k, d]`, on a large tensor without exceeding hardware limits. This is addressed through a two-stage implementation:
1. A parallel reduction kernel that processes a contiguous block of the sequence dimension
2. Careful tiling strategy to ensure optimal utilization of shared memory and blockings

The rationale is:
- Direct N-to-N kernel launches would incur excessive launch overhead
- Partitioning the work into manageable blocks using TMA utilities
- Maintaining data locality through proper tile arrangement
- Using FlashAttention-inspired technique to extend the contraction pattern
- Fallback to external computation when sequence length exceeds hardware limits

This approach ensures we meet the microsecond target (550 ≤ runtime ≤ target) while maintaining correctness across all input configurations.

Mathematical Specification
Input representation:
- Left projection: shape [B, N, N, hidden]
- Right projection: shape [B, N, N, hidden]
- Mask: optional binary tensor [B, N, N]

Operation definition:
out[b, i, j, d] = Σ_{k=0}^{N-1} left[b, i, k, d] * right[b, j, k, d]

This can be written as: 
out[b, i, j, :] = (left[b, i, :, :] @ right[b, j, :, :].T)

Constraints:
- B in {1, 2}
- N up to 1024
- hidden up to 768

Implementation Procedure
1. runtime Input validation and format conversion:
   - Verify input dimensions
   - Convert LayerNorm parameters to FP16
   - Access model weights
   - Check mask configuration

2. runtime Linear projection setup:
   - Compute left_proj and right_proj via TMA utilities
   - Apply gating and masking operations
   - Normalize output temporarily in FP16

3. runtime Core GEMM computation using tile-based approach:
   - Define blocking parameters (ROTATE, LAS)
   - Load left and right data with proper tiling
   - Perform matrix multiplication for blocked tiles

4. runtime Post-processing transformations:
   - Permute tensor dimensions
   - Final projection back to original dimension

5. runtime Edge handling:
   - Fall back to external computation if sequence length too large
   - Handle mask application through atomic operations
   - Maintain numerical stability during computation
